newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Weaker Indonesian rupiah seen raising inflation.
newsitem.headline: Weaker Indonesian rupiah seen raising inflation.

text.p: Indonesia's inflation rate is likely to rise following the rupiah's sharp fall against the U.S. dollar, National Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita was quouted as saying by the Observer newspaper on Monday.

"It is impossible for us to say that inflation will not rise...this year, as a result of the change in the exchange rate, there will (be) several costs which will go up," he was quoted as telling reporters on Sunday. He gave no details.
President Suharto said on Saturday the country's inflation rate fell to 6.5 percent last year from 8.6 percent in 1995. The government aims to cap inflation at 6.0 percent this year.
The rupiah fell to a historic low of 2,960 against the dollar on Friday and was trading at 2,925/45 at 0300 GMT on Monday.
